title: Rebuild the Approval Queue around one kind of page, a document

calls.question: How long does a merged pull request stay on the front page?

options.label: Seven days
options.consequence: Each merged line shows under its tool's name for seven days, then drops off the page. The store keeps it.

options.label: Until you mark the section as read
options.consequence: Lines pile up until you clear them, and the page needs one more button.

options.label: Since the previous day only
options.consequence: This is what the mockup showed. A merge you didn't open the queue for within a day is never listed.

evidence.text: The mockup listed merges "since yesterday", and the design says a fixed window is simpler to reason about.

decidedForYou.question: Where is the new queue built while you keep using the old one?

options.label: In a directory beside the old app, with the first five passes landing without a packet
options.consequence: Nothing you use changes until the sixth pass. Each of the five lands after its gate run passes and its whole-branch review is accepted, and you see one sentence per merge.

options.label: In place, pass by pass
options.consequence: The queue you approve with changes under you five times, and each pass needs a packet.

evidence.text: The design's order of passes and how each lands.

decidedForYou.applied: In a directory beside the old app, with the first five passes landing without a packet

decidedForYou.question: How does an approve reach the session, given the one that was lost?

options.label: The server records it first, and hands it to the session 20 seconds later
options.consequence: The page changes only after the server has the decision on disk. Undo works for those 20 seconds, and the page says when the session has it.

options.label: The browser holds it for the Undo window, as today
options.consequence: This is the behavior that lost your approve on 2026-11-12.

evidence.text: What happened to the approve, and the new order of events.
Backlog #71 records the lost approve in your words.

decidedForYou.applied: The server records it first, and hands it to the session 20 seconds later

decidedForYou.question: What happens to the old queue's decided items?

options.label: They go into one archive file, and the new queue starts empty
options.consequence: `restart` writes `~/.local/state/approval-queue/archive-2026-11.tar.gz` only after the new server answers. You said you don't need to look at old decided packets.

options.label: The new queue shows them read-only
options.consequence: The new code would carry a reader for every old item shape.

evidence.text: The archive step and its order.

decidedForYou.applied: They go into one archive file, and the new queue starts empty

decidedForYou.question: What is the command written in?

options.label: TypeScript, sharing the document library with the pages
options.consequence: One parser decides what a document is, for the command and the page alike. The 1,124-line bash command is retired at the switch.

options.label: Bash, as today
options.consequence: The command and the pages would each parse a document, and could disagree.

decidedForYou.applied: TypeScript, sharing the document library with the pages

steps.text: After the weekly usage reset on 2026-11-13, 11pm Anchorage time, launch the round's conductor from `plans/aq-rewrite-conductor-prompt.txt`. Its first pass waits for the workstation round's fix to the busy check (workstation backlog #75). If the workstation design is sent back, this round can't start until that fix is approved some other way.
Read one close packet, in the old queue, once the sixth pass and the workstation round are ready. It carries the switch.

notChecked.text: No pass has parsed the five real documents with the planned library. The mockup's parser did, and pass A1 parks if the library can't.
Vale has not read this design. The house config's scope excludes the record's folder. `tellgrader` under the docs register reports nothing.
The repo runs no CI, so each pass's own gate run is the only automated check.
The edits made after the builder check were not read by a second fresh reader.

reviews.text: One builder check by a fresh Opus reader read both designs against the queue's code and the workstation's skills and returned fifteen findings. Each was folded as Claude's call, and none needed your answer.
